# A6d results (generated by highz_2017.py; do not edit)

Editorial analysis. Genzel's baryonic accelerations come from NFW halo fits. The Eq. 8 results below are conditional on those inputs; a no-halo QI refit to the measured kinematics remains open.

QI scale today a_Q(0) = 2c²/Θ₀ = 2.043 × 10⁻¹⁰ m s⁻² (Θ₀ = 8.8 × 10²⁶ m).

The circular acceleration is below the Fig. 2 reference in 5 of 6 galaxies (n=1 radius). McCulloch's Eqs. 5–8 include a varying component a′ as well as ordered rotation; the latter can be below 2c²/Θ. This count is not a violation of Eq. 8 or of the combined-acceleration floor.

## Übler et al. 2017 baryonic Tully–Fisher relation (dex of mass at fixed velocity)

Eq. 13 assumes slow rotation at the outskirts (McCulloch Sect. 4, Eqs. 10–13). Übler Sect. 2.3–2.4 uses maximum circular velocities near 2.2 R_d. This reproduces the author's comparison without establishing the deep-limit approximation for that sample.

| z | observed bTFR offset from local | observed sTFR offset | McCulloch's quoted range | QI Eq. 13, relative to QI at z = 0 | QI absolute, relative to the SPARC normalisation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.9 | -0.44 | -0.44 | -0.38 to -0.47 | -0.28 | -0.51 |
| 2.3 | -0.27 | -0.42 | -0.20 to -0.47 | -0.52 | -0.75 |

Within Übler's sample, z ≈ 0.9 → 2.3: observed bTFR zero point changes by +0.17 ± 0.06 dex; the Eq. 13 deep-limit formula gives -0.24 dex (difference 6.4 times the quoted statistical error). This is an arithmetic discrepancy in that comparison, not a calibrated QI exclusion significance. Übler's alternative samples give +0.28 and +0.20 dex.
